presets.decision: Follow transmission from South Asia to Central, East and Southeast Asia. Keep anonymous devotional objects and the Dhammapada. The First Buddhist Council has unknown local dates and must remain unplaced; Maurya, Han and Tang supply dated context.

Follow interconnected Eurasian and Mediterranean regions, not one modern nationality. Han, Tang, Song, Mongol and Byzantine periods establish exchange context; conquest and plague are explicitly contextual. Country matching is an introductory survey, not evidence that each object travelled the routes.

Retain the existing country OR recorded Byzantine-tradition scope. A hard country/creator intersection would exclude anonymous icons and mosaics held abroad; show the reviewed geographic/tradition scope instead. Remove Highlights to retain museum-supported objects.

Include Abbasid Iraq and Iran, Central Asia, North Africa and al-Andalus. Keep anonymous manuscripts and objects; religious/conquest events establish historical context and are not themselves claims of scientific achievement. Additional dated intellectual milestones remain a coverage gap.

Use China and its separately recorded historical dynasties; anonymous calligraphy, ceramics and paintings remain discoverable. Tang and Northern Song are the available dated core events; Mongol expansion is aftermath. Southern Song event coverage remains incomplete.

Include Mali and the wider West African/Saharan trade network, preserving unnamed makers. The local event sequence currently supplies only Mali Empire; Ghana, Songhai and Timbuktu need sourced dated records. Do not fill this gap with unrelated Mediterranean events.

sources.name: The Met — Sahel: Art and Empires
